description: Introduces 2025 budget adjustments, proposing a 5.2% property tax.
Details investments in police, transit, and roads.

chips.text: Councillor Davies noted this budget was the best start in 12 years, reducing it before kickoff.
Saskatoon's population grew by 46,000 residents since 2018, projected to 2025.

description: Presents 2025 preliminary budget with 5.2% tax increase.

chips.text: Received as information
11 for, 0 against
Council discussed starting 2025 budget deliberations at 5.2% instead of 5.84%.
Council may further reduce the preliminary tax increase during deliberations.

description: Saskatoon Public Library levy increases 2.8% for 2025.
Police Service adds 24 new frontline officers.
City's major venues and services continue operations.

chips.text: Approved
11 for, 0 against
Mayor Block emphasized housing vulnerable people improves community safety.
Police will create a dedicated warrant enforcement team.
Provincial funding for 24 police officers is a once-in-a-generation opportunity.
Residents expressed strong concerns about crime and safety.
Police flagged a pending binding arbitration award for wages.
Remai Modern offers low-sensory events for children with autism.
Remai Modern developing its first environmental plan.
Police will hold a special meeting for wage recommendation by December 18.

description: Committee recommends renewing Nutrien Wonderhub's lease, phasing in facility cost increases.
City provides $250,000 annual in-kind support via below-market rent.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor Garner questioned the market value of Wonderhub's current rent
Families and children use the museum, impacted by admission fees and exhibit quality.
No concrete plan exists for Wonderhub's proposed revitalization of the Civic Conservatory.
Wonderhub's Executive Director requested Option 4
Wonderhub stated new charges for repairs and insurance could contravene the lease agreement.

speakers.name: Chief Financial Office Hack
speakers.summary: Chief Financial Office Hack presented the report and responded to questions of Council.
said: Administration recommends phasing in facility cost increases over five years.
Current rent is below market value, an annual $250,000 in-kind contribution.
City provided $2M for construction, $95K annual grant, and below-market lease.

description: Material Recovery Centre had 23,000 visits in its first year.
Generated over $240,000 revenue from material sales and stewardship.
Four additional staff are still needed for full service delivery.

chips.text: Approved
11 for, 0 against
Centre expands waste diversion opportunities for various materials.
Administration will report on staffing needs before 2026-2027 budget deliberations.

description: Adds two Fire Bylaw Inspectors and a vehicle, costing $181,500.

chips.text: Approved
11 for, 0 against
Impacts services at the Emergency Wellness Centre.

description: Saskatoon will explore permanent public washrooms in Riversdale and Pleasant Hill.
Interim options could extend North Cawanis washroom pilot to 2025.
City will develop a long-term strategy for public washroom access.

chips.text: Approved
11 for, 0 against
Comfy trailer pilot evolved into a navigation center, helping users find housing and employment.
Lack of 24/7 washroom access impacts unhoused individuals and their neighbors.
City staff committed to developing a long-term public washroom access strategy in 2025.

description: Information provided on extending 8 spray pads and Riversdale Pool.
Two-week spray pad extension costs $50,400; pool costs $69,600.
Spray pads can extend quickly; pool needs advance notice.

chips.text: Approved
11 for, 0 against
Councillor praised administration for extending spray pads in 2024.

description: Saskatoon's 2025 budget proposes 74.4 new city positions.
Forty-one new positions are for Saskatoon Police Service.
New staff will support city growth and services.

chips.text: Approved
11 for, 0 against
Councillor Donauer explained city operations differ from businesses regarding COVID impacts.
Community members questioned the number of city employees and budget adjustments.

description: Saskatoon's debt is projected to peak at $442 million in 2026.
City debt remains low compared to other municipalities.
Four 2025 budget projects require borrowing approval.

chips.text: Approved
11 for, 0 against
Administration will provide further reporting on debt projections.

description: Approves $125,000 for 2025 Accessibility Plan project.

chips.text: Approved
11 for, 0 against
$125K to be funded from RCE
Addresses accessibility barriers for residents and employees due to new Act.

description: Recommends 4.96% property tax increase for 2025.
Adds $500,000 to snow budget, funds fire inspectors.
Approves WonderHub operating costs for five years.

chips.text: Recommended
That the 2025 Operating Plan approved by City Council on November 28, 2023
Councillor Parker raised concerns about underfunding asset management plans.
Councillor Donnar preferred a lower snow budget increase than approved.
Legal dispute exists over WonderHub lease costs and interpretation.
Fire bylaw inspectors support unhoused individuals and community safety.
Councillor Davies committed to more transit safety staff next year if needed.
